title: arXiv Physics — Thursday, 5 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart, readership, or download ranking. This is an inferred notable-paper ordering; the announcement batch is too recent for useful age-normalized citation momentum, and citation evidence is limited. The ordering is not a popularity measure.

sections.title: Gravitational-Wave Constraints on $R^2$ Gravity
sections.abstract: The authors derive a theory-specific inspiral-waveform correction for quadratic f(R) gravity and use two binary-neutron-star events to constrain its curvature coupling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a combined 90%-credibility bound a ≲ 6.2×10^6 m² (equivalently m_s ≳ 3.2×10^-11 eV), about five orders of magnitude tighter than the previous best astrophysical bound.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Bayesian waveform analyses of GW170817 and GW190425
sections.unique_caveat: The analysis omits R²-induced changes to neutron-star structure, which the authors identify as future work; the constraint depends on waveform and stellar-structure assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-archive cross-listing, a quantified two-event gravitational-wave constraint, and two separate secondary synopsis pages (weak attention signal, not expert validation).

sections.title: Cryogenic suppression of correlated loss in Rydberg atom arrays
sections.abstract: The authors compare room-temperature and cryogenic Rydberg atom arrays and find that suppressing blackbody radiation suppresses avalanche-driven correlated atom loss.
sections.claimed_result: A 45 K shield suppresses blackbody-driven decay by up to 30–50% (effective radiation temperature about 190 K) and lowers avalanche rates by up to 22% for tested Rydberg states.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; cryogenic/room-temperature Rydberg arrays up to 70 atoms, lifetime and correlated-loss measurements, and a rate model
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstrated arrays contain at most 70 atoms and the shield's effective blackbody temperature is about 190 K; further suppression toward 45 K is projected, not demonstrated. Photoionization and laser phase noise also contribute.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-archive cross-listing and a controlled experimental comparison with a quantitative rate model tested against measured loss.

sections.title: The M87 Black Hole Mass from JWST and Keck Stellar Kinematics Spanning 10 pc to 10 kpc
sections.abstract: The authors combine JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI stellar-kinematics maps with triaxial orbit modeling to infer M87's central black-hole mass across a wide radial range.
sections.claimed_result: The authors infer M_BH=(5.38±0.13±0.22)×10^9 M☉ and report a mass-to-distance ratio whose 90% credible interval overlaps the multi-epoch EHT interval.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST NIRSpec and Keck KCWI stellar kinematics analyzed with triaxial Schwarzschild orbit models
sections.unique_caveat: The statistical uncertainty is smaller than the systematic uncertainty from M87's adopted distance; the EHT comparison uses existing EHT results, not a new EHT measurement.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two observatories provide contiguous kinematic coverage; the analysis fits about 5,000 constraints and compares its mass-to-distance ratio with independent EHT results.

sections.title: New Neutron Polarizabilities from Deuterium Compton Scattering at HI$\gamma$S
sections.abstract: A 61 MeV deuterium Compton-scattering measurement at HIγS, analyzed with chiral effective field theory, yields updated neutron electric and magnetic scalar polarizabilities.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain α^n_E1=12.25±1.1(stat)±0.3(BSR)±0.8(th) and β^n_M1=2.95∓1.1(stat)∓0.3(BSR)∓0.8(th), in 10^-4 fm³, reducing statistical uncertainty by 12% versus the prior extraction.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; 61 MeV photons on liquid deuterium at HIγS, NaI(Tl) detectors, and χEFT analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The extraction depends on χEFT and the Baldin sum-rule constraint; the quoted theoretical uncertainty is 0.8×10^-4 fm³, and the result is statistically consistent with the previous extraction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: New facility-based measurements separate elastic and inelastic events and yield explicit polarizability estimates with statistical, BSR, and theory uncertainties.

sections.title: DESI DR2 Results III: The Mass of the Milky Way
sections.abstract: The DESI Collaboration applies four dynamical methods to 10,036 halo stars in DR2 and combines mock-calibrated estimates of the Milky Way's mass.
sections.evidence_type: observational and computational; DESI DR2 six-dimensional halo-star data calibrated with cosmological mock surveys
sections.unique_caveat: The correction depends on mock-based treatments of disequilibrium, selection functions, and method- and tracer-specific biases.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: DESI Collaboration key-project analysis uses 10,036 stars, compares four methods on mock surveys, and models residual correlations between methods.

sections.title: Experimental activation of hidden metrological steerability in quantum channels via stochastic filtering
sections.abstract: The authors demonstrate that stochastic pre- and post-filtering can restore violation of a metrological steering inequality in a photonic amplitude-damping channel.
sections.claimed_result: The critical damping parameter for violating the metrological steering inequality rises from about 0.5 to about 0.75 at the strongest tested filter setting.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; polarization qubits in a two-path Sagnac amplitude-damping channel, with Brewster-angle glass-plate filtering
sections.unique_caveat: The advantage is conditional on probabilistic filtering, which lowers success probability; the experiment tests amplitude damping rather than arbitrary noise channels.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct photonic experiment with a quantified change in the noise threshold, extending stochastic filtering to an operational metrological-steering witness.

sections.title: Search for GeV-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
sections.abstract: The LHCb Collaboration updates its search for axion-like particles produced by exclusive photon fusion in forward PbPb collision data and reports limits across 3–10 GeV.
sections.claimed_result: Using 0.228 nb^-1 of PbPb data at √s_NN=5.02 TeV, the collaboration probes masses to 3.0 GeV and couplings to 3.2×10^-4 GeV^-1, with strongest limits from 3 to 5 GeV.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; LHCb forward-detector analysis of PbPb collision data
sections.unique_caveat: This is a search limit, not a detection; sensitivity is specific to recorded luminosity, forward acceptance, and the assumed exclusive production and decay channel.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A v2 replacement was announced in this batch; it is the authors' first forward search for exclusive γγ→a→γγ and provides explicit mass/coupling reach.

sections.title: Near-Quantum-Limited Readout for the Princeton Axion Search using a sub-GHz Kinetic Inductance Traveling Wave Parametric Amplifier
sections.abstract: The authors characterize a kinetic-inductance traveling-wave parametric amplifier for low-noise readout between 300 and 700 MHz.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report over 30 dB gain at 300–700 MHz and measured system noise of 2.5–3.5 quanta.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; amplifier characterization with a variable-temperature noise source
sections.unique_caveat: This is an amplifier-performance study, not an axion detection; performance is established for the reported band and measurement configuration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-archive cross-listing and quantified sub-GHz gain/noise measurements for precision readout applications.

sections.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). Refining the strong lens sample with Space Warps crowd-sourced science
authors: N. E. P. Lines et al.
sections.abstract: Using Euclid Q1 lens candidates, the authors assess volunteer confidence grading against researchers and how calibrated volunteer probabilities might refine future samples.
sections.claimed_result: Volunteer grading can be calibrated against researchers; a conditional Q1 rerun could reach 79% completeness and 41% purity for Grades A+B before researcher inspection.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Euclid Q1 lens-candidate images graded by Space Warps volunteers and researchers
sections.unique_caveat: The completeness/purity figures are conditional rerun estimates, not a realized release result; substantial disagreement remains for intermediate-grade candidates.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Euclid collaboration data, manuscript submitted to A&A, and quantified citizen-science classification analysis with implications for the Q1 sample.

sections.title: Simulating a chiral gauge theory
sections.abstract: The authors construct a finite-dimensional, gauge-invariant lattice formulation for 1+1-dimensional Abelian chiral gauge theories and simulate the 34-50 model with infinite matrix product states.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report that a finite local Hilbert space with N=6 reproduces the expected infrared c=1 behavior of the 34-50 model in a thermodynamic-limit simulation.
sections.evidence_type: computational; clock-and-shift qudit lattice model simulated with infinite matrix product states and compared with analytic benchmarks
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration is for 1+1-dimensional Abelian theories and a finite-N lattice construction; extension to higher dimensions, non-Abelian theories, or real-time dynamics is not demonstrated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-archive cross-listing and a computational method preserving discrete chiral symmetry/anomaly, with simulated infrared properties compared against analytic predictions.

sections.title: Quantum Noise Spectroscopy of Criticality in an Atomically Thin Magnet
sections.abstract: The authors use NV-center spin-decoherence noise magnetometry on trilayer CrSBr to measure critical fluctuations and infer dynamical and correlation-length exponents.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report Ising-like critical behavior that deviates from short-range Ising and XY predictions, attributing the deviation to long-range dipolar interactions and easy-axis anisotropy.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and computational; NV-center T2 noise magnetometry on trilayer CrSBr interpreted with simulated noise models
sections.unique_caveat: The universality-class interpretation depends on the noise model and a single material/thickness; tests across samples and control parameters are needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A v3 replacement announced in this batch; NV-center noise measurements, simulations, quantitative critical exponents, and cross-listing between condensed matter and quantum physics.

sections.title: Hall-Density Collapse as Direct Evidence for Percolative Conduction Onset in Monolayer MoS$_2$ Transistors
authors: C. J. L. de la Rosa
sections.abstract: Temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on monolayer MoS2 transistors with amorphous HfO2 dielectrics are presented as evidence that disorder-driven percolation explains conduction onset.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify a temperature-independent Hall-density collapse and vanishing activation energy at a characteristic carrier density as signatures of a classical percolation threshold in the studied devices.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; temperature-dependent transport and Hall measurements on monolayer MoS2 field-effect transistors
sections.unique_caveat: The conclusion is tied to the studied MoS2/amorphous-HfO2 device system; the abstract does not establish that this mechanism dominates other two-dimensional electron systems.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Two complementary transport signatures address a debated interpretation of apparent metal-insulator transitions; the manuscript is marked submitted to Physical Review Letters.
